pathway.title: CACI INTERNATIONAL INC /DE/ — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. CACI's leverage stepped up with the March 2026 acquisition and has only partly eased. Total debt to EBITDA was 3.04x at FY2025, 4.20x at FY2026 and 3.94x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 2.93x, 4.04x and 3.72x [CP-1 financial base]. The acquired business entered earnings for under seven months of that latest period while its financing is fully in debt, so the reported ratio may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of the effect is Not supplied because no pro forma earnings are given [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary]. Credit implication: leverage tolerance is the main variable, and it improves only if cash flow after interest is applied to debt.

2. CACI's liquidity is strong and its near-term maturity profile is light. Cash was USD 279.389 million and the undrawn revolver USD 1,395.0 million at September 30, 2026; scheduled maturities are USD 46.750 million in FY2027 and no more than USD 78.000 million a year until FY2031, when USD 1,706.750 million falls due, with USD 2,959.250 million after that [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: refinancing risk sits in FY2031 and beyond, and the revolver matures in November 2030. The receivable sale program is close to its USD 350.0 million cap and its stated term ends on December 18, 2026, so it should not be counted as spare liquidity [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary].

3. CACI's cash generation covers its interest comfortably on a historical basis. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.67x in FY2025, 5.49x in FY2026 and 5.60x on the latest twelve months, and operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 775.961 million on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base]. The quarterly cash interest figure omits semi-annual note coupons, and the income statement interest charge for the latest quarter exceeds cash paid, so the historical cover will not hold if the interest run-rate stays at the higher level [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate but the cushion has narrowed since FY2025.

4. CACI depends on a single payer, which concentrates funding and contract risk. Federal customers were 95.6% of FY2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6%, and the ten largest contracts 22.5%; the government may terminate contracts for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the government fiscal year only through December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1A timeline]. Credit implication: revenue visibility from the USD 34.0 billion backlog is conditional on funding and option exercise, and only USD 6.2 billion is funded [CP-1A company and operating model].

5. CACI's contract mix is moving toward more fixed-price work. Fixed-price revenue was 33.2% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 26.7% a year earlier, and cost-plus-fee fell from 60.5% to 52.8% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Mechanism: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Countering evidence: management EBITDA margin rose from 11.7% to 13.3% between the two first quarters [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: earnings variability rises with execution, offset so far by margin gains.

6. CACI's creditor protections cannot be verified. The senior secured instruments (revolver, term loans) total USD 3,364.438 million of floating-rate principal with swaps covering USD 1,400.0 million notional, and USD 1,500.0 million of senior unsecured notes sit beside them [CP-1 financial base]. Covenant levels, definitions, guarantors and baskets are Not supplied; management states compliance with all financial covenants, which is an attributed claim [CP-0; CP-1A governance table]. Credit implication: headroom and default distance cannot be sized, and ranking by entity is not assessable.

7. Subsequent events are mixed. The Board approved a calendar fiscal year on October 20, 2026, so the next report covers a six-month transition period; the litigation judgment was vacated on October 21, 2026, though plaintiffs may seek further review; and fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on October 21, 2026 [CP-1A timeline; CP-1A conflicts]. Credit implication: period comparisons will change and a USD 42 million contingent claim has eased but is not closed.

runs.text: Strengths. First, revenue is almost entirely federal and backlog-supported, which gives revenue visibility in normal budget conditions [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Second, liquidity is ample: cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,674.389 million against light scheduled amortisation [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Third, cash generation is solid, with operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 775.961 million and cash interest cover of 5.60x on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-supportive on the record: no dividend has been paid, share repurchases were cut and the revolver balance fell from USD 660.0 million to USD 605.0 million in the latest quarter [CP-1A governance table] (Documentary Fact). Fifth, the margin trend is positive, with management EBITDA margin of 13.3% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 11.7% a year earlier [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Management describes its execution as a differentiator, which is Management Language and is not adopted here [CP-1A company and operating model] (Management Language).

Weaknesses. First, leverage is higher after the acquisition, at 3.94x total debt to EBITDA on the latest twelve months against 3.04x at FY2025, and the effect of acquired earnings is unquantified [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact; the overstatement of run-rate leverage is Analyst Interpretation). Second, payer concentration and funding risk: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience and a continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Third, fixed-price work is growing as a share of revenue, which transfers cost-overrun risk to the company [CP-1A company and operating model] (Analyst Interpretation). Fourth, floating-rate exposure: USD 1,964.438 million of floating-rate principal is not covered by swap notional, so higher rates would raise cash interest and lower cover [CP-1 financial base] (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, the company is an active acquirer, with eight acquisitions in three fiscal years and a preliminary purchase price allocation for the latest, so leverage depends on future deal appetite [CP-1A governance table] (Analyst Interpretation). Sixth, the receivable sale program is at its cap with a stated term ending December 18, 2026 [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Seventh, covenant terms, guarantors and ownership are not supplied, which limits the assessment and is not an adverse finding in itself [CP-0; CP-1A company profile] (Insufficient Information).

runs.text: The principal transaction is the acquisition of ARKA Group L.P., which closed on March 9, 2026 under a purchase agreement and plan of merger dated December 19, 2025, among a CACI operating subsidiary, the issuer, a merger subsidiary, the target and two other limited partnerships (10-K exhibit index, page:104). The 10-K states purchase consideration of 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, subject to post-closing adjustments, that the acquisition is intended to enhance the ability to deliver advanced technology for national security customers in the space domain, and that it was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand (10-K page:79). The allocation recorded 1,145.0 million of intangible assets and 1,462.9 million of goodwill (10-K page:80). The target's sellers, any sponsor or minority interest and any earnout are not described in the supplied text, which is an Insufficient Information item. A smaller acquisition of a data and cloud migration business by the U.K. subsidiary closed on February 17, 2026 for 10.7 million net of cash acquired (10-K page:81). Management reports post-acquisition revenue of 166.8 million and net income of 17.4 million for the two businesses together in FY2026, after 26.0 million of intangible amortisation (10-K page:81); this is a partial-period contribution and not a run-rate figure. In the latest quarter the consideration was reduced to 2,637.7 million after a 5.0 million purchase price refund from the final working capital settlement, and the allocation is still preliminary (Q1 10-Q page:5). The two figures are logged as a conflict of versions below and are not reconciled here.

New debt linked to the transaction. On March 9, 2026 the company amended its Term Loan B agreement to add a 800.0 million seven-year senior secured Term Loan B-2 (10-K page:88, page:89). On March 12, 2026 it issued an additional 500.0 million of its 6.375% senior unsecured notes due June 2033, forming part of the same series as the 1,000.0 million notes issued on June 2, 2025, at a premium, with net proceeds of 516.5 million used to repay revolver borrowings (10-K page:89). A senior secured bridge loan commitment of up to 1,300.0 million dated December 19, 2025 was never drawn and was terminated on March 9, 2026 (10-K page:81). Earlier and related financing events: the Term Loan B of 750.0 million on October 30, 2024; the 1,000.0 million notes of June 2, 2025, whose net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings; and the November 25, 2025 amendment of the senior secured credit facility, made primarily to extend its maturity (10-K page:88, page:89). Revolver borrowings also funded part of the price: the revolver was drawn 928.0 million at March 31, 2026 and 605.0 million at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 base). Liquidity effect: cash and undrawn revolver stood at 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 per the CP-1 base.

Status and subsequent events. The acquisition is closed; the allocation is preliminary; the purchase agreement text, the credit agreement amendments and the indenture supplements are named in the exhibit index but are not supplied, so conditions, guarantors and covenants for the new debt are Not supplied. The fiscal-year change (October 20, 2026), the vacated judgment (October 21, 2026), the raised guidance (October 21, 2026) and the receivable program term ending December 18, 2026 are subsequent events or future contract terms, not FY2026 facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI is a Delaware holding company whose operating subsidiaries provide technology and expertise to national security customers, with essentially all revenue from the U.S. federal government. The view for a creditor is that business risk is dominated by funding and contract-structure mechanics rather than by market competition: revenue visibility comes from a large backlog but depends on annual appropriations and on contracts that the government may terminate for convenience; margin resilience depends on the contract mix, which moved toward fixed-price work in the latest quarter; and cash conversion depends on receivable collection and on a receivable sale program that is nearly at its cap and has a stated term ending in December 2026. The one transformative transaction in the record is the March 2026 acquisition of a space-domain technology business, financed with an 800.0 million term loan tranche, a 500.0 million add-on of senior unsecured notes and revolver borrowings, after which the revolver balance has fallen. Ownership is public and dispersed on the evidence supplied, but control rights and holder concentration are Not supplied because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and is not in the pack. No sponsor behaviour can be assessed because none is named. The record shows no dividend ever paid and sharply reduced share repurchases in FY2026. The fiscal-year change disclosed on October 20, 2026 and the October 2026 court developments are subsequent events and are kept out of FY2026 facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The principal transaction is the acquisition of ARKA Group L.P., which closed on March 9, 2026 under a purchase agreement and plan of merger dated December 19, 2025, among a CACI operating subsidiary, the issuer, a merger subsidiary, the target and two other limited partnerships (10-K exhibit index, page:104). The 10-K states purchase consideration of 2,642.7 million net of cash acquired, subject to post-closing adjustments, that the acquisition is intended to enhance the ability to deliver advanced technology for national security customers in the space domain, and that it was funded from increased borrowings and cash on hand (10-K page:79). The allocation recorded 1,145.0 million of intangible assets and 1,462.9 million of goodwill (10-K page:80). The target's sellers, any sponsor or minority interest and any earnout are not described in the supplied text, which is an Insufficient Information item. A smaller acquisition of a data and cloud migration business by the U.K. subsidiary closed on February 17, 2026 for 10.7 million net of cash acquired (10-K page:81). Management reports post-acquisition revenue of 166.8 million and net income of 17.4 million for the two businesses together in FY2026, after 26.0 million of intangible amortisation (10-K page:81); this is a partial-period contribution and not a run-rate figure. In the latest quarter the consideration was reduced to 2,637.7 million after a 5.0 million purchase price refund from the final working capital settlement, and the allocation is still preliminary (Q1 10-Q page:5). The two figures are logged as a conflict of versions below and are not reconciled here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt linked to the transaction. On March 9, 2026 the company amended its Term Loan B agreement to add a 800.0 million seven-year senior secured Term Loan B-2 (10-K page:88, page:89). On March 12, 2026 it issued an additional 500.0 million of its 6.375% senior unsecured notes due June 2033, forming part of the same series as the 1,000.0 million notes issued on June 2, 2025, at a premium, with net proceeds of 516.5 million used to repay revolver borrowings (10-K page:89). A senior secured bridge loan commitment of up to 1,300.0 million dated December 19, 2025 was never drawn and was terminated on March 9, 2026 (10-K page:81). Earlier and related financing events: the Term Loan B of 750.0 million on October 30, 2024; the 1,000.0 million notes of June 2, 2025, whose net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings; and the November 25, 2025 amendment of the senior secured credit facility, made primarily to extend its maturity (10-K page:88, page:89). Revolver borrowings also funded part of the price: the revolver was drawn 928.0 million at March 31, 2026 and 605.0 million at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 base). Liquidity effect: cash and undrawn revolver stood at 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 per the CP-1 base.

fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience, backlog of 34.0 billion of which 6.2 billion is funded (10-K page:12, page:8; Q1 10-Q page:20). Mechanic: appropriations, continuing resolutions and option exercise determine conversion of backlog to cash; a lapse in funding delays awards and collections for all agencies at once. Implication: revenue is durable in normal budget conditions but its stress case is a funding disruption, not competition; the nearest dated exposure is the continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026. Countering item: a book-to-bill of 2.0x in the latest quarter, although contract awards were below the prior-year quarter (Q1 FY2027 release pages:1, 9).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share up from 26.7% to 33.2% and cost-plus-fee down from 60.5% to 52.8% between Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 (Q1 FY2027 release page:8). Mechanic: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Implication: earnings and cash flow become more variable with execution; this is a year-over-year change in one quarter, and a counter-signal is the higher EBITDA margin reported for Q1 FY2027 in the CP-1 base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Acquisition and leverage mechanics. Evidence: 2,642.7 million consideration funded by borrowings, 800.0 million term loan, 500.0 million notes (10-K pages:79, 88, 89). Mechanic: debt arrived before a full period of acquired earnings, so reported leverage in the CP-1 base is not a run-rate figure. Implication: deleveraging depends on cash flow after interest and on future acquisition appetite; conflicts logged above affect the price but not the financing amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CACI's fundamental credit profile is sound but more leveraged after its March 2026 acquisition, resting on a federally funded business that converts earnings into cash. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,674.389 million at September 30, 2026 against scheduled debt maturities of USD 46.750 million in FY2027, with EBITDA covering cash interest 5.60x over the twelve months to that date. The weakest point is leverage of 3.94x total debt to EBITDA, in a business that relies on one payer and on government funding and termination conditions. The outcome depends on deleveraging from cash flow while federal funding stays orderly; covenant terms and guarantors are not disclosed in the supplied sources and remain unverified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. CACI's leverage stepped up with the March 2026 acquisition and has only partly eased. Total debt to EBITDA was 3.04x at FY2025, 4.20x at FY2026 and 3.94x on the twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 2.93x, 4.04x and 3.72x [CP-1 financial base]. The acquired business entered earnings for under seven months of that latest period while its financing is fully in debt, so the reported ratio may overstate run-rate leverage; the size of the effect is Not supplied because no pro forma earnings are given [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary]. Credit implication: leverage tolerance is the main variable, and it improves only if cash flow after interest is applied to debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. CACI's liquidity is strong and its near-term maturity profile is light. Cash was USD 279.389 million and the undrawn revolver USD 1,395.0 million at September 30, 2026; scheduled maturities are USD 46.750 million in FY2027 and no more than USD 78.000 million a year until FY2031, when USD 1,706.750 million falls due, with USD 2,959.250 million after that [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: refinancing risk sits in FY2031 and beyond, and the revolver matures in November 2030. The receivable sale program is close to its USD 350.0 million cap and its stated term ends on December 18, 2026, so it should not be counted as spare liquidity [CP-1 financial base; CP-1A transaction summary].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. CACI's cash generation covers its interest comfortably on a historical basis. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.67x in FY2025, 5.49x in FY2026 and 5.60x on the latest twelve months, and operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 775.961 million on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base]. The quarterly cash interest figure omits semi-annual note coupons, and the income statement interest charge for the latest quarter exceeds cash paid, so the historical cover will not hold if the interest run-rate stays at the higher level [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate but the cushion has narrowed since FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. CACI depends on a single payer, which concentrates funding and contract risk. Federal customers were 95.6% of FY2026 revenue, the Department of War 53.6%, and the ten largest contracts 22.5%; the government may terminate contracts for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the government fiscal year only through December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model; CP-1A timeline]. Credit implication: revenue visibility from the USD 34.0 billion backlog is conditional on funding and option exercise, and only USD 6.2 billion is funded [CP-1A company and operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. CACI's contract mix is moving toward more fixed-price work. Fixed-price revenue was 33.2% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 26.7% a year earlier, and cost-plus-fee fell from 60.5% to 52.8% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Mechanism: the contractor bears cost overruns on fixed-price work and loses automatic inflation pass-through. Countering evidence: management EBITDA margin rose from 11.7% to 13.3% between the two first quarters [CP-1 financial base]. Credit implication: earnings variability rises with execution, offset so far by margin gains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. CACI's creditor protections cannot be verified. The senior secured instruments (revolver, term loans) total USD 3,364.438 million of floating-rate principal with swaps covering USD 1,400.0 million notional, and USD 1,500.0 million of senior unsecured notes sit beside them [CP-1 financial base]. Covenant levels, definitions, guarantors and baskets are Not supplied; management states compliance with all financial covenants, which is an attributed claim [CP-0; CP-1A governance table]. Credit implication: headroom and default distance cannot be sized, and ranking by entity is not assessable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Subsequent events are mixed. The Board approved a calendar fiscal year on October 20, 2026, so the next report covers a six-month transition period; the litigation judgment was vacated on October 21, 2026, though plaintiffs may seek further review; and fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on October 21, 2026 [CP-1A timeline; CP-1A conflicts]. Credit implication: period comparisons will change and a USD 42 million contingent claim has eased but is not closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, revenue is almost entirely federal and backlog-supported, which gives revenue visibility in normal budget conditions [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Second, liquidity is ample: cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,674.389 million against light scheduled amortisation [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Third, cash generation is solid, with operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 775.961 million and cash interest cover of 5.60x on the latest twelve months [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-supportive on the record: no dividend has been paid, share repurchases were cut and the revolver balance fell from USD 660.0 million to USD 605.0 million in the latest quarter [CP-1A governance table] (Documentary Fact). Fifth, the margin trend is positive, with management EBITDA margin of 13.3% in the first quarter of FY2027 against 11.7% a year earlier [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Management describes its execution as a differentiator, which is Management Language and is not adopted here [CP-1A company and operating model] (Management Language).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, leverage is higher after the acquisition, at 3.94x total debt to EBITDA on the latest twelve months against 3.04x at FY2025, and the effect of acquired earnings is unquantified [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact; the overstatement of run-rate leverage is Analyst Interpretation). Second, payer concentration and funding risk: 95.6% federal revenue, termination for convenience and a continuing resolution ending December 11, 2026 [CP-1A company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). Third, fixed-price work is growing as a share of revenue, which transfers cost-overrun risk to the company [CP-1A company and operating model] (Analyst Interpretation). Fourth, floating-rate exposure: USD 1,964.438 million of floating-rate principal is not covered by swap notional, so higher rates would raise cash interest and lower cover [CP-1 financial base] (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, the company is an active acquirer, with eight acquisitions in three fiscal years and a preliminary purchase price allocation for the latest, so leverage depends on future deal appetite [CP-1A governance table] (Analyst Interpretation). Sixth, the receivable sale program is at its cap with a stated term ending December 18, 2026 [CP-1 financial base] (Documentary Fact). Seventh, covenant terms, guarantors and ownership are not supplied, which limits the assessment and is not an adverse finding in itself [CP-0; CP-1A company profile] (Insufficient Information).
